title: Is it possible to create Wide Sprite s for Battlers or Walking Sprite s? Also, other Sprite questions..

posts.author: willowwisp
posts.body:
I know that it's possible to make tall sprites, but I'm wondering if it's possible to make sprites that are wide (for example: 56 px wide and 48 px tall), specifically as sprites that will follow the player character around?
Secondarily; if I were wanting to make a dragon battling game, is there a way to make randomised pieces of sprites (different horns and wings, for instance)?
Thirdly; what's the largest size of Battler you can have that still kind of.. makes sense, on the player's side? especially if there's going to be multiple of them?
Sorry for the lots of questions, I'm new to this and my fiancee and I are planning to make a game together, and I wanted to get started on making the sprites but I'm not sure where to start.. any help is appreciated!!

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
Hello and welcome! If you're new to the forum, please make sure familiarize yourself with the
Support Template
. With that out of the way:
willowwisp said:
I'm wondering if it's possible to make sprites that are wide
Click to expand...
No problem making the sprites wide. Press F1 when inside the editor, and choose
Documentation > Asset Standards > Image Assets
Here you will find what the format of the various sprite sheets is. Also look up the included top view sprites (folder img/characters). The included sprites are 48 x 48 per cell and have 12 columns by 8 rows, so the full sprite sheet will be 576 by 384 pixels. If you wanted sprites that are 56 x 48, your full sprite sheet would be 672 by 384 pixels.
willowwisp said:
is there a way to make randomised pieces of sprites (different horns and wings, for instance)
Click to expand...
I'm not sure what you mean.
willowwisp said:
what's the largest size of Battler you can have that still kind of.. makes sense, on the player's side?
Click to expand...
IMO, optimal battler size depends on many factors, such as the screen resolution of your game, how much you intend for the characters to move during combat, and how much UI real estate you will have in your combat screen. Probably easiest to experiment with different sized placeholders to give you an idea. The default battlers are 64px tall, I use sprites that are 96px tall (1 foot of height= 16 px), but I've also seen larger sprites with the default resolution.
It's recommended to work your way through the tutorials first, that can be accessed from Help in the menu bar. Have fun and good luck!

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body: For your second part, you can make multiple different versions of your troops and enemies with the variations you want. Unless I'm misunderstanding what you are trying to achieve.

posts.author: willowwisp
posts.body: Thank you both! For the second part, what I mean is; I want to create a Drake species; this species can have varying patterns, horn types, ear types, pupil shapes, and spine shapes. Is there a way, with me making custom assets of each part, for the game to make randomised versions of sprites with these different parts?

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
willowwisp said:
Is there a way, with me making custom assets of each part, for the game to make randomised versions of sprites with these different parts?
Click to expand...
Well, all the JavaScript is right at your fingertips, so essentially anything is
possible
. But I have only seen this implemented in a limited fashion. I suppose you could also create your own character generator assets, but that will be quite an investment of your time. I'd just create the patterns manually. If you really want it you can always commission someone to make a plugin for it.
